corrections.claim: chatPrompt in server/prompt.go silently truncates messages that exceed num_ctx, so a 9k-token observation is cut unless the context is at least 16384.
corrections.source: Ollama tag v0.40.7 (commit 2cd63f7a, cloned): server/prompt.go lines 20-92; llm/llama_server.go lines 299-336, 338-348; server/sched.go lines 172-190; api/types.go line 1225 read 2026-10-22.
corrections.correctValue: The conclusion stands but the mechanism is wrong. chatPrompt only drops OLDER messages and always keeps system messages and the last one, so for our request (one system message from `instructions` plus one user message) it never removes anything. The silent cut happens in llama_server.go completionPromptForRequest: with Truncate (default true) and context shift (resolveContextShift defaults true for every model except deepseek2) an over-long prompt has its MIDDLE discarded, keeping the first num_keep=4 tokens and the tail and cutting down to about half of num_ctx (contextShiftPromptLimit = numCtx - max((numCtx - numKeep)/2, 1), so about 8,194 tokens kept at 16,384), with only a server-log warning ('truncating input prompt') and no HTTP error. With shift off it would return 400 promptTooLong. I read only this /completion path; models without an Ollama renderer go through llama-server's chat endpoint, whose truncation I did not read. /v1/responses cannot set truncate or shift.

corrections.claim: (Omission in the research) Context length and overflow behaviour for llama-server.
corrections.source: llama.cpp tag b11799 (commit 0756e83f, cloned): tools/server/README.md line 50 (-c default 0 = taken from the model), line 171 (--context-shift default disabled), line 177 (-np default auto); tools/server/server-context.cpp lines 3948-3956 (message string at line 3950) read 2026-10-22.
corrections.correctValue: Set -c explicitly: the default is the model's training context (131,072 for gpt-oss, 262,144 for the others), which would allocate far more KV than the 16k assumed. With context shift off (the default) an over-long request is REJECTED with 'request (N tokens) exceeds the available context size (C tokens), try increasing it' (ERROR_TYPE_EXCEED_CONTEXT_SIZE), so llama-server does not truncate silently, unlike Ollama. Use -np 1 so the slot gets the whole -c.

schemaFit.detail: Schema analysis is in the 'SCHEMA ANALYSIS' note: every construct is inside the llama.cpp converter subset except bakerPrice.price number min/max, which is silently unenforced and caught by validateDecision (protocol.ts:86-87). Path: text.format.schema -> ChatRequest.Format -> llama-server json_schema; the grammar starts after the Harmony final-channel header (harmony/harmonyparser.go 469-477). Needs temperature:0 in the body, since Ollama otherwise forces 1.0. reasoning.effort 'low' is a native gpt-oss level. Not tested live.

The schema is inside the converter's subset, but whether llama-server applies the response_format grammar only after the analysis channel for gpt-oss was neither read nor tested. The transport also needs a new adapter (response_format:{type:'json_schema', json_schema:{name, strict, schema}}, max_tokens, reasoning_effort) pointed at a non-OpenAI address.

notes: SCHEMA ANALYSIS (common to every local model; checked against llama.cpp common/json-schema.cpp build_node and grammars/README.md lines 205-216, identical in b11738 and b11799). Supported and used by us: objects with additionalProperties:false and every property required (enforced); one-value typed enums {type:'string',enum:[x]} and {type:'number',enum:[3]} (the enum node is checked before type); 16-hex string enums (strings() is only built from non-empty lists, guarded in mockProvider.ts, so no 'enum must be a non-empty array' failure); anyOf [{type:'null'}, ...] with no sibling keys on any anyOf node (nullable() and referent return only {anyOf}); nested anyOf communication > proximityUtterance > referent and context (children are built recursively); a bare {type:'null'} property. Not used by us, so no exposure: type arrays, $ref, allOf, pattern, length bounds, const. The single weakened construct is bakerPrice.price {type:'number', minimum:0, maximum:2}: the documented subset enforces min/max only for integer, so the grammar allows any number silently; validateDecision rejects price outside [0,2] (src/agent/protocol.ts:86-87), so an out-of-range price becomes a failed decision, not an impossible one. The id enums change every call, so a new grammar is built per call; its cost was not measured.

EXCLUDED FROM SURVIVORS. Ministral-3-14B Q8_0: weights 14.36 GB + 2.68 GB KV = 15.87 GiB, no room for compute buffers or Windows (fit confirmed NOT possible). Gemma-4-26B-A4B QAT: 13.96 GiB before compute buffers and Windows, no throughput data, so neither the fit nor the 12,000 ms cap can be shown; not established, left out rather than refuted. LM Studio and vLLM: no verified path to text.format on a Responses body (LM Studio) or no native Windows (vLLM).

METHOD. Read 2026-10-22, about 02:00-02:50 UTC. No new research: I did not look for models, providers or runtimes beyond the researcher's list. I read the saved result field, then fetched each cited source directly: raw.githubusercontent.com and shallow git clones at the exact tags (Ollama v0.40.7 = 2cd63f7a, llama.cpp b11799 = 0756e83f, plus b11738 raw copies for diffing, vLLM v0.32.0 raw files), the Hugging Face API at the cited commits, localscore.ai, lmstudio.ai, ai.google.dev and PyPI. A few spot checks of the researcher's exclusion claims used HF listings. No paid model call was made. I used the add_repo tool for ollama/ollama and ggml-org/llama.cpp; it only confirmed anonymous git read access.

NOT READABLE IN THIS SESSION (403 'GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session'): GitHub release pages, the releases API and atom feed, and github.com/.../discussions. So these claims stay unverifiable: which Ollama release is flagged Latest or pre-release, Ollama's Windows asset list, and llama.cpp discussions #15013 and #15396. Release ASSET downloads on github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp did answer (HEAD), so the llama-server Windows zips were checked.

BOTTOM LINE ON THE RESEARCH. Every hash, size, commit, config value, licence, release tag and source-file claim I could reach matched. Corrections: (1) Ollama v0.40.7 was not released on 18 Oct (tag commit is 2026-10-20) and a v0.40.8 final tag already exists; (2) the silent-truncation mechanism is context-shift middle-discard in llama_server.go, not chatPrompt; (3) 'the existing transport works with Ollama' is only true of the loopback fixture function, not the production path. Omissions with real consequences: Ollama /v1/responses forces temperature 1.0 and overrides the Modelfile, so repeatability needs temperature:0 in the body; our fixed reasoning.effort 'low' switches thinking ON for Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 under Ollama; llama-server defaults to port 9931, temperature 0.80, and -c = the model's training context, so -c, --temp, -np, --alias and --port must all be passed; and the repo caps every call at 12,000 ms, not ~16 s.

INSTALL CHECKLIST, OLLAMA (pin v0.40.7, commit 2cd63f7a, bundles llama.cpp b11738). (a) Do not install 'latest'. (b) Set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384 (default is 4096 under 24 GiB; the body can be up to 32,768 bytes plus 2,048 output tokens) or `PARAMETER num_ctx 16384` in the Modelfile. (c) Overflow is silent: middle tokens are discarded keeping the first 4 and the tail; only the server log shows 'truncating input prompt'. Log usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens and the prompt token count and compare them to the expected size. (d) Prompt caching cannot be disabled (cache_prompt:true is hard-coded at llm/llama_server.go lines 1691 and 2299), so bitwise repeatability is not guaranteed. (e) Create the model from the pinned GGUF (`FROM ./file.gguf`) after checking sha256, and give it a name matching /^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$/. (f) Body changes needed for any repeatable or thinking-off run: temperature:0; for Qwen3.5/Gemma 4 reasoning.effort 'none' or think:false. (g) Fixed sampling that Ollama will not override: seed in the Modelfile. (h) The only existing transport that can reach 127.0.0.1:11434 is the loopback fixture.

INSTALL CHECKLIST, LLAMA-SERVER (b11799, commit 0756e83f). Assets: llama-b11799-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip (272 MB) or -cuda-13.4-x64.zip (160 MB) plus the matching cudart-llama-bin-win-cuda-<12.4|13.4>-x64.zip (391 MB / 424 MB). Verified flags (tools/server/README.md): -m, -c N (default 0 = model training context, always set it), -np 1, -ngl (auto/all/N), -fa [on|off|auto], --temp 0, --no-cache-prompt, --host (default 127.0.0.1), --port (default 9931), --alias (needed so the model id passes the regex), -rea off / --reasoning-budget 0 for thinking models, --reasoning-effort, -s/--seed, --context-shift (default disabled; leave it off so an oversize prompt errors instead of truncating). Use /v1/chat/completions with response_format {type:'json_schema', json_schema:{name, strict, schema}}; /v1/responses ignores text.format. -fit defaults to on; since -c is set explicitly it should not shrink it, but I did not verify that interaction.

SCHEMA, ALL LOCAL RUNTIMES. Every construct we use is inside the llama.cpp subset except the price bounds (number min/max is documented as unsupported and is silently ignored). Whatever the runtime, validate every output client-side; validateDecision already does for price. Nothing in the research or here shows a live request with this schema being accepted by a local runtime.

WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED. Real throughput of any listed model on the RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (all timings are the researcher's estimates), real VRAM use including compute buffers and Windows, Ollama's handling of a raw-GGUF Modelfile for thinking models (parser/renderer/thinking metadata), grammar plus empty-thought-block behaviour for Gemma 4, the grammar-after-analysis behaviour of llama-server for gpt-oss, and whether Ollama v0.40.7 actually loads the Gemma 4 12B 'unified text' architecture. Run `llama-bench -m <file> -ngl 99 -fa 1 -p 9000 -n 300 -r 3` and then time real requests end to end, including grammar overhead, before committing to a model.
